title: Cohesion and Coupling
definition: Cohesion describes how strongly a unit's elements serve one responsibility; coupling describes how much separate units depend on each other's data, state, timing, or internal decisions.
purpose: Compare decomposition alternatives by change cost, test isolation, and contract clarity.
history: Cohesion and coupling are established software-design qualities; exact taxonomies and metrics vary, so beginner assessment uses observable dependency evidence.
mental_model: A cohesive tool has one clear job; loosely coupled tools connect through small labeled interfaces rather than shared hidden machinery.
analogy: Specialized teams with written handoffs; unlike software, people can resolve ambiguity informally, so explicit contracts remain essential.
common_mistakes: Counting calls as the only coupling
Using shared mutable state for reuse
industry_notes: The goal is appropriate coupling through stable contracts, not zero dependency.
ai_notes: Ask for dependency inventory and independent test plan, not subjective clean-code claims.
interview_notes: Ask candidates to compare two valid boundaries using change scenarios.
